workHeading.title: Selected work
workHeading.description: Fan experiences. Consumer products. Enterprise systems. A few places where thoughtful engineering makes a difference.
workHeading.exitHint: Keep scrolling to see how I work ↓

projects.title: Williams F1 Team
projects.summary: A connected fan platform across web and mobile, with personalized Williams IDs, loyalty, and race-day experiences.
projects.imageAlt: Alex Stopa Williams ID fan card with customized helmet and loyalty progress, screenshot provided by Alex
projects.role: Technical lead at Slytrunk: frontend architecture, shared platform systems, and technical direction for a team of 4–5 engineers.
projects.challenge: Build a connected fan experience across web, mobile, content, and the moments that matter on race weekend.
projects.approach: My work spans the multi-tenant platform’s architecture, frontend systems, and technical direction. I help engineers and stakeholders align around practical decisions, with a consistent fan identity across touchpoints.
projects.outcome: A shared platform that connects the fan experience while supporting the needs of different teams and leagues.
projects.mediaNote: Williams ID: fan identity, customization, and loyalty.

projects.title: Healthline
projects.summary: A high-traffic consumer publishing platform that makes health information accessible to a broad audience.
projects.imageAlt: Current Healthline article interface, captured directly from an interior article page
projects.role: Contributing engineer at Slytrunk, delivering features within Healthline’s existing web platform.
projects.challenge: Deliver features within a large, high-traffic consumer platform, where the interface needs to make complex information approachable.
projects.approach: My work included feature delivery on Healthline.com as part of the Slytrunk team. It brought my engineering experience into a consumer platform with substantial existing scale and complexity.
projects.outcome: Experience working within a high-traffic product, alongside the smaller teams and early-stage products that also shape my approach.
projects.mediaNote: Current article layout and reading experience.

projects.title: Trash Panda
projects.summary: A mobile food scanner that helps people understand ingredients and find alternatives while shopping.
projects.imageAlt: App screenshots pending: scan results, ingredient details, swaps and shopping lists
projects.role: Contributing engineer at Slytrunk, delivering app features with frontend and backend capabilities.
projects.challenge: Help people make sense of food information through an approachable consumer product.
projects.approach: I contributed to feature delivery for the Trash Panda Food Scanner app, bringing frontend and backend capabilities to an early-stage product.
projects.outcome: A useful example of the work I enjoy: turning complicated information into something people can understand and use.
projects.mediaNote: Native app: scanning, ingredient information, and shopping.

approach.title:
Deep in the technology.
Clear with the people.
approach.intro: The best technical solution only works if people understand why it’s the right one. I connect those two worlds.
approach.technical: A multi-tenant, event-driven architecture with shared services and tenant-specific configuration.
approach.human: One strong foundation. A distinct experience for every client. Less rebuilding, more moving forward.

items.title: Find the real problem.
items.body: Ask better questions. Understand what the business needs and what people actually need to do.

items.title: Make the tradeoffs clear.
items.body: Explain the options, the constraints, and the consequences in language everyone can work with.

items.title: Build it to hold up.
items.body: Thoughtful architecture, fast interfaces, and maintainable systems. Then help the team carry it forward.

about.title: An engineer with a communicator’s instinct.
about.body: My degree is in Communications. My career is in software. That combination shapes how I work: I care as much about a shared understanding as I do about a well-designed system.
about.second: At Deloitte, that meant translating complex technical work for enterprise stakeholders. At Slytrunk, it means connecting product ambitions, engineering decisions, and the people building them.

history.description: Leading a team of 4–5 developers. Architecting web, mobile, CMS, and backend systems for a multi-tenant fan engagement platform.
Leading delivery of enterprise applications, serverless systems, fraud dashboards, and tools that turn complex data into useful decisions.
Building and maintaining websites while creating content across newsletters, social, and email. Where technology and communication first came together.

experiment.title: An experiment in AI-assisted building.
experiment.body: I’m using this site to explore where AI helps, where it falls short, and where human judgment makes the difference.
